subject: Post-demo recap: vendor contrast, decision checklist & next tests
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Morgan Hill <morgan@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: vendor contrast, decision checklist & next tests

Hi Morgan —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick written recap so we have alignment and a clear set of next steps. I tried to keep this short and actionable.

Key pain / goals you called out
- Latency-sensitive summarization pipeline for call transcripts (95th pct < 250ms per token end-to-end)
- On-prem / VPC option for PHI workloads and audit trails
- Predictable per-token economics at scale (projected 2–3B tokens/month)

Decision criteria we heard you weight heavily
1) Latency predictability (hard SLO)
2) Data residency & auditability (SOC2 + enterprise KMS)
3) Cost at scale (unit economics)
4) Model fidelity for clinical summarization (domain benchmarks)

What we demonstrated today
- Live generation with our hosted API and a dedicated deployment sketch
- KV cache behavior and initial latency numbers on our synthetic transcript workload
- Migration plan for on-prem/VPC with minimal client-facing changes

Attachments (first pass)
- contrast_matrix_v1.xlsx — side-by-side of Redwood vs two competitors on the criteria above
- poa_test_plan.md — suggested POC test suite (latency probes, model parity prompts, KV cache warmup)

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Your confirmation of decision owners and weighting (who will sign off on latency vs cost tradeoffs)
2) Redwood provides the POC test plan + baseline latency report by EOD Wednesday (we'll run the same prompts shown in demo)
3) Schedule a 3-week POC window (week of 8/31) with a brief kickoff and two technical checkpoints
4) NDA / procurement templates (if you want, we can send a redline-ready starter)

Open questions for you now
- Do you need an on-prem appliance or is a private VPC with dedicated instances sufficient for the first phase?
- Will Priya (security lead) be on the POC kickoff? If so, we'll include KMS and audit log endpoints in test scope.

If that looks right I'll get the team to run the first set of latency tests and share the baseline report.

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0147
[Attachment: contrast_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 112KB)]
[Attachment: poa_test_plan.md (text, 8KB)]

From: Morgan Hill <morgan@helixhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@medisync.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: vendor contrast, decision checklist & next tests

Thanks Logan — this is helpful and captures the discussion. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: 95th < 250ms is a hard bar for the real-time summarizer. If you can show real measurements on a 5–10k user simulated burst that would be ideal.
- Data residency: VPC with customer-managed KMS is preferred initially. On-prem appliance is only necessary if we can't meet SOC2 + audit needs in the VPC option.
- Stakeholders: Priya (cc'ed) will own the security QA. I'll loop in Chris (CTO) for the commercial decision once we have the POC baseline.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood include a short pricing sensitivity table showing Dedicated reserved vs hosted over 12 months?
2) We need to see model parity for 10 sample clinical prompts — are you comfortable running those in the POC?

We'll aim to confirm the POC window by EOD tomorrow.

—Morgan
Morgan Hill
Director of Platform Engineering, Helix Health
morgan@helixhealth.com | +1 617-555-0190

Hi Morgan / Logan —

Quick technical note from the SE perspective and what we'll run during the POC if you confirm. I'm attaching a short test plan (poa_test_plan.md) but high-level: 

POC technical probes (priority order)
1) Latency burst test: 5k concurrent user-simulated bursts with 4k-token transcripts, measure end-to-end 50/95/99 percentiles across three regions
2) KV cache warmup / cold starts: ensure first-request cold miss behavior vs warmed cache, and quantify delta
3) Model parity: we'll run your 10 clinical prompts + 20 mixed prompts against the same open model variants (ours vs competitor B) and compare BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics and a small set of domain-specific scorers you provide
4) Security & audit validation: KMS integration, retention settings, and a short trace of request-level audit events in the private control plane

Data we'll need from you to run parity tests- 10 example prompts (anonymized) and expected outputs or acceptance criteria- Preferred VPC region and whether test traffic should originate from your corp IPs

I'll schedule the first baseline run tomorrow morning (Wed 8/19) unless you prefer a later start.

Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | (650) 555-0222
[Attachment: poa_test_plan.md (text, 8KB)]

Hey Morgan — adding a short competitive snapshot and a pricing sensitivity table so you can see tradeoffs quickly. The attached PDF (redwood_vs_competitor_snapshot.pdf) includes an apples-to-apples on reserved Dedicated vs hosted and a simple example of cost at 2B tokens/month.

A couple of commercial notes: 
- We can offer a pilot credit for the POC (covers up to 100M tokens) to reduce friction on your side.
- For Dedicated reserved capacity we typically structure a 12-month commit with quarterly checkpoints — if you commit to a minimum baseline we can pass through a modest discount.

Let's plan to sync after the first baseline latency run so we can iterate on the test plan.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole

1) Please share an NDA link or redline-ready starter before kickoff.
2) We'll provide the 10 anonymized clinical prompts by Friday (8/21).
3) Chris (CTO) will join the kickoff if the baseline latency report meets the 95th<250ms target.

—Morgan
